name: Zanzibar pilau
subtitle: Pilau is a spiced rice dish of the Swahili coast; its name, like 'pilaf', comes from the Persian polow.

facts.label: Name and origin
facts.value: The name pilau, like pilaf, derives from the Persian polow, rice mixed with spices, nuts and meat

facts.label: History
facts.value: The dish is linked to the Indian Ocean spice trade and Arab settlers in East Africa

facts.label: Zanzibar style
facts.value: The Zanzibar version is made with coconut milk and without tomato or raisins

facts.label: Spices
facts.value: Pilau masala: cardamom, black pepper, cinnamon and cloves

facts.label: When eaten
facts.value: Very hard to miss at any Tanzanian celebration; more heavily spiced than the Indian version

facts.label: Variations
facts.value: People in the coastal region add cashew nuts

facts.label: Where
facts.value: Spiced pilau is among the traditional Swahili dishes served at a Stone Town restaurant

parts.text: Pilau is a spiced rice dish of the Swahili coast; its name, like 'pilaf', comes from the Persian polow. Rice, preferably basmati, is cooked with onion and a spice mix of cardamom, black pepper, cinnamon and cloves, and a Zanzibar version is made with coconut milk.

It is a fixture of Tanzanian celebrations, served with kachumbari salad, and appears among the traditional Swahili dishes in Stone Town eateries; cooks may add meat, seafood, vegetables or, on the coast, cashew nuts.

blocks.title: Zanzibar Pilau (Rice Pilaf)
blocks.sub: One version of the dish, as given by Connecticut Public (excerpt from In Bibi's Kitchen, Ten Speed Press 2020); the steps are summarised in our own words. Recipes differ from cook to cook.
blocks.note: From Hawa Hassan's In Bibi's Kitchen, reprinted by Connecticut Public. Soaking time is 10 to 30 minutes; resting time at least 10 minutes.

steps.text: Rinse the rice in a sieve under cold water, stirring gently, until the water is clear.
Leave the rice to soak in a bowl of cold water (10 to 30 minutes).
Meanwhile melt the butter in a medium pan over medium-high heat and soften the onion.
Add the cardamom, cinnamon and cloves and stir until fragrant.
Pour in the coconut milk, boiling water and salt, then add the drained rice.
Cover, turn the heat to low and cook until the liquid is absorbed and the rice tender.
Leave covered off the heat, then fluff, pick out the whole spices and serve hot.
